title: Verbal Intelligence
shortDescription: Vocabulary, comprehension, similarities and general information, based on the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS).
longDescription: Verbal Intelligence measures overall verbal intellectual functioning across five WAIS-inspired subtests: Vocabulary, Comprehension, Similarities, General Information, and Arithmetic Reasoning.
sourceNote: Ported verbatim from airostudio/verbalize — 40 real questions across the 5 real WAIS-inspired subtests found in the source.

sections.name: Vocabulary
sections.description: Assesses knowledge of word meanings and verbal comprehension of individual terms.
sections.instructions: Select the definition that best matches the given word.

sections.name: Comprehension
sections.description: Assesses practical judgment, reasoning about social conventions, and understanding of common sayings.
sections.instructions: Choose the answer that best explains the reasoning or meaning behind the statement.

sections.name: Similarities
sections.description: Assesses abstract verbal reasoning by identifying conceptual relationships between two items.
sections.instructions: Choose the answer that best describes how the two items are alike.

sections.name: General Information
sections.description: Assesses fund of general knowledge across geography, history, science, and the arts.
sections.instructions: Select the correct answer to each general knowledge question.

sections.name: Arithmetic Reasoning
sections.description: Assesses numerical reasoning and the ability to solve word problems involving calculation and logic.
sections.instructions: Solve each problem and select the correct answer.

scoringDimensions.label: Verbal Intelligence
scoringDimensions.description: Composite score reflecting overall verbal intellectual functioning across vocabulary, comprehension, similarities, general information, and arithmetic reasoning.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Your verbal intelligence score suggests foundational verbal skills are still developing across vocabulary, comprehension, and reasoning tasks.
recommendations: Build vocabulary daily by learning and using 3-5 new words
Read a variety of material, including nonfiction and opinion pieces
Practice explaining idioms and proverbs in your own words

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Your verbal intelligence falls within the typical range, showing solid but improvable skills in language and reasoning.
recommendations: Engage in discussions or debates to sharpen verbal reasoning
Read above your comfort level to expand vocabulary
Practice solving word problems to strengthen arithmetic reasoning

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: You demonstrate strong verbal intelligence, with solid command of vocabulary, comprehension, and abstract reasoning.
recommendations: Challenge yourself with advanced literature or essays
Try writing persuasive arguments to refine eloquence
Explore general knowledge quizzes to broaden your base

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: You show very strong verbal intelligence, excelling in word knowledge, judgment, and conceptual reasoning.
recommendations: Mentor others in writing or verbal communication
Pursue complex reading such as academic or philosophical texts
Continue practicing multi-step reasoning problems to stay sharp

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Your verbal intelligence is exceptional, reflecting outstanding vocabulary, comprehension, abstract reasoning, and general knowledge.
recommendations: Pursue advanced writing, debate, or public speaking opportunities
Consider fields that leverage strong verbal-analytical ability
Keep exploring diverse topics to maintain your broad knowledge base
